meta.scope: Seasonal, evergreen micro-insights shown one per day. All factual; no dollar amounts invented.

items.text: January: pull a free credit report at annualcreditreport.gov. You're entitled to one free report per bureau every week.
Tax season opens late January. Gather W-2s/1099s — employers must send them by Jan 31.
February: many states' property-tax 2nd installment is delinquent around Apr 10. Check your county treasurer now.
March: IRA contributions for the prior year can still be made until Tax Day. Last chance to lower last year's tax bill.
April 15: federal Tax Day for most. An extension gives time to file, not to pay — interest accrues from the original due date.
Open enrollment for health insurance ends mid-January; a qualifying life event (marriage, birth, move, job loss) can open a Special Enrollment Period.
May: review withholdings after filing. If you got a big refund or owed a lot, adjust your W-4 to better match the year.
June: many states' fiscal year starts July 1 — city minimum wages and local taxes often change then. Re-check your locality.
July 1: a wave of city minimum wages (CA, DC, others) increases. If you earn tips, confirm your new local cash wage.
August: if you're self-employed, the Q3 estimated-tax deadline (Sep 15) is about six weeks out — start setting aside now to avoid the 0.5%/month IRS penalty.
September 15: Q3 estimated tax due for the self-employed. Mark it before the quarter ends.
October: Open Enrollment for ACA Marketplace begins Nov 1. Preview plans and subsidies at HealthCare.gov.
November 1: ACA Open Enrollment starts. Premium tax credits are based on income — a mid-year raise can change your subsidy.
December 31: deadline for many tax-year moves — HSA, FSA, 529, and charitable gifts must be made by year-end.
Year-end: energy-efficiency federal credits (heat pump, solar, insulation) generally require the upgrade placed in service by Dec 31.
